episodes.206468: A troughing pattern from the Pacific brought in a late season monsoon burst of moisture to the Desert Southwest. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over portions of the state with more locally heavy rainfall events occurring from the abundant monsoon moisture. Flash flooding was observed in several locations ranging from near El Malpais south of Grants, NM, in Navajo Nation west of Crownpoint, and in Tijeras east of Albuquerque. One woman was reportedly swept away from flash flooding south of Gallup near Red Rock.
episodes.206522: An early season low pressure system moved into southeastern California and cut off from the main steering flow.  Leftover monsoon moisture from the subtropics combined with the stalled low pressure system and brought a 4 day period of severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.206617: A trough to the west, coupled with the effects of moist upslope flow, helped trigger scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across far West Texas and Southeast New Mexico throughout the day on September 28th. While no severe weather was reported, ample moisture and terrain effects resulted in at least one instance of flash flooding in the Davis Mountains and one instance of flooding due to runoff near Carlsbad.
episodes.206951: A fairly weak cutoff low slowly ejected northward through the area over the course of several days. This feature in combination with sufficient moisture created an environment that supported several days of shower and thunderstorm development. Some of these storms produced locally heavy rainfall and flash flooding, as well as some strong wind gusts.
episodes.207295: A slow-moving low pressure system brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms over multiple days through much of the region. Activity on the 25th was mostly concentrated across higher terrain areas of eastern AZ, fueled by MLCAPE values approaching 2000 J/kg. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours, producing rainfall accumulations of over 2 inches in less than one hour across the Miami area leading to significant flash flooding. Multiple streets became rushing currents of water, floodwaters escaped Bloody Tanks Wash in several locations and flooded businesses, there was a lot of muddy and rocky debris, and there were several minor landslides. Severe hail was observed with the thunderstorm activity as well. ||The most impactful day of this multi-day episode occurred on the 26th when widespread thunderstorm activity developed across much of south-central AZ as strong upper-level divergence from the low pressure system moved overhead. Fueled by MLCAPE values near 2000 J/kg and near 30 kts of 0-6 km shear, scattered thunderstorms developed in the Phoenix area during the mid-morning hours with increasing coverage through the afternoon hours. Initially, most of the storm reports received were large hail, however, as activity became more widespread the hazard quickly turned to flash flooding with numerous reports of water rescues. A fatality due to drowning was reported in Indian Bend Wash in Scottsdale when the individual's vehicle became submerged by significant floodwaters. A few hours after the rainfall dissipated in the Phoenix area, a new area of strong to severe thunderstorms, with very heavy rainfall, moved eastward into southern Gila County, affecting the Globe/Miami area for a second time in just over 24 hours. Gauge reports and doppler radar estimates out of the Globe area measured approximately 2��� of rain, with most of the rain occurring in less than 30 minutes. A stream gauge along Pinal Creek, just south of downtown Globe, reported a 6 foot water rise in 30 minutes. Subsequently, videos and images emerged from downtown Globe depicting catastrophic flooding as the flood wave in Pinal Creek overtopped bridges, inundated businesses, and flooded or swept away numerous vehicles. Around 800 propane tanks were also swept into the floodwaters from a nearby distribution center. Around 66 vehicles were recovered and approximately 288 tons of trash and debris, as well as 8000 cubic yards of dirt, were cleared.  The flooding claimed three lives. ||Additional shower and thunderstorm activity materialized on the 27th as the low pressure system was still over southern CA. The more widespread activity was concentrated across portions of southwest AZ during the morning and early afternoon hours with instances of flash flooding reported. Additional activity did develop across south-central AZ as well, including across portions of the Phoenix area, during the afternoon hours. Coverage was more isolated compared to the 26th, but the storms still produced additional flash flooding and severe winds gusts. A thunderstorm cell once again moved through the already flood ravaged area of Globe/Miami in the afternoon. Despite rainfall amounts remaining under an inch with this storm, due to quick storm motion, flash flooding occurred once again in the area, exacerbated by the very saturated soils from the rainfall the previous two days.||Following this three-day episode, local, state, and federal disaster declarations were made for the Globe area, a disaster assistance center was opened, and approximately 600 initial and preliminary damage assessments were conducted by AZ Department of Emergency and Military Affairs, finding around 200 private and public properties were destroyed, with the rest experiencing some scale of damage. Not all events are captured in detail in this episode due to the large scale and number of the impacts. Damage cost estimates were in the millions.
episodes.207555: A large cluster of thunderstorms moved offshore from the Everglades, producing an area of gale force wind gusts across the middle Florida Keys coastal waters as they progressed southward from Florida Bay to the Straits of Florida side.
episodes.207703: A negatively tilted trough was moving through southern California and northern Baja which tapped plenty of subtropical moisture.  Locally heavy rain developed along the east slopes of the Blacks Range and brought flash flooding and wind damage to the Monticello area.
episodes.207712: A late season monsoonal moisture push into the Rio Grande Valley combined with an upper trough moving northeast through the Four Corners region brought heavy rain and flash flooding to the Hueco Tanks area.
episodes.207872: Low pressure moved very slowly east from the eastern Pacific across the Mojave Desert, triggering scattered thunderstorms for a few days. Several storms produced flash flooding.

events.narrative: Yucca Mesa Road was flooded with water and debris.
Downed power line reported between Madison and Jackson Streets and between 12th and 14th Streets. No injuries reported.
Estimated wind gust of 55-60 mph near the corner of Thomas Road and 48th Street in Phoenix. No injuries or damage reported.
Reports of power pole down along 19th Street, in between Washington and Jefferson Streets in Phoenix.

Several very large trees were uprooted in a neighborhood located in the area of 24th street and Thomas in Phoenix. One tree fell onto the roof of a house, damaging the roof, while another tree fell onto a vehicle. Wind gusts were estimated at around 70 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

The AZ Ice Arcadia Rink located in the area of 38th street and Thomas Road in Phoenix suffered significant damage, with the roof of the building partially peeled off and damage that led to an electrical fire. Dust and debris fell from the damaged roof/ceiling onto the rink and everything else inside. The building's TV satellite dish was also thrown onto the roof of the building next door. Wind gusts, given the severity of the damage, were estimated at around 70 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported. Damage estimates were reported at approximately $1 million.

Numerous downed power lines in a large area between North 24th to North 40th street and Osborn Road to Red Mountain Freeway in Phoenix. Over 6000 homes were without power. Wind gusts were estimated up to 70 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

Footage from near the Home Depot and Walmart in the Desert Palms Shopping Center, located at 36th Street and Thomas Road in Phoenix, showed approximately 20-30 downed trees in the parking lot. Wind gusts were estimated upwards of 70 mph. No injuries reported.

Downed power lines in the area of North 44th Street and Camelhead Road and Camelback Road to Campbell Avenue in Phoenix. Wind gusts were estimated at 55-60 mph. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
ASOS at Phoenix Deer Valley Airport measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph. No damage or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gauge along Indian Bend Wash at Shea Boulevard recorded a water level above the alarm stage level of 2 feet, with the stage peaking at 3.02 feet and likely flooding the downstream greenbelt area of the wash and low water crossings. Timing estimated based on the period when water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage level. No damages or injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge along Jackrabbit Wash recorded a water level above the alarm stage level of 2.9 feet, with a peak stage of 3.78 feet. Exceeding alarm stage corresponds to likely flooding of Wickenburg Road located approximately 5.1 miles downstream of the gauge. There was an extended period of greater than 900 cfs with flow peaking at 1560 cfs, resulting in likely greater than 1.5 feet of flowing water over the road. Timing estimated based on the period when water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage level as well as travel time for the water to reach Wickenburg Road. No damages or injuries reported.
Water rescue along North 40th Street due to flooding in Cudia City Wash. No injuries reported.

A Flood Control District of Maricopa County streamflow gauge on Skunk Tank Wash at 7th Ave recorded a water level above the designated alarm stage of 4.2 ft and reached a peak stage height of 5.48 ft at 1940MST. With water levels above alarm stage, multiple low water crossings became impassable. Timing based on when water level rose above and fell below alarm stage. No damages or injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge along Sonoran Wash recorded a water level above the alarm stage of 2.0 feet, and peaked at a stage of 3.57 feet. Based on the peak stage level, the unbridged crossing at North Valley Parkway was likely flooded based on studies and mapping by the flood control district. Timing estimated based on the period when water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage level as well as travel time for the water to reach North Valley Parkway. No damages or injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge along Cave Creek Wash measured a water level above the alarm stage level of 3 feet, and reached a peak stage of 3.65 feet. Based on the peak stage 7th Avenue was likely impassable, based on studies and mapping by the flood control district. Timing estimated based on the period when water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage level. No damages or injuries reported.
Social media video showed evidence of mud flows and damage from flash flooding near the town of Monticello.
Social media report showed snapped power poles around Monticello as well as a damaged barn.
Rainfall over the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding that washed out a low water crossing along Maple Drive through Brady Canyon.

Repeated rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall resulted in standing water estimated up to a foot deep over an estimated one tenth of a mile stretch of highway along NM 13 at mile marker 29 approximately six miles west of U.S. Highway 285.

A delayed report was received of flash flooding between the Buffalo Trail Boy Scout Camp and State Highway 17. Roads leading into the camp were reported to be impassible, especially at low water crossings. The camp itself did not flood. The time of occurrence is  partially estimated from radar. No damage was reported.
Video clips from Oatman, AZ, showed fast-flowing water and mud over the Oatman Highway near mile marker 23.
The county stream gauge at Mayer (54936 - Big Bug Creek @ SR 69) reported a 4.4 ft rise in 30 minutes, peaking at 1:55 pm.
Reports on social media and by the NM DOT showed pictures of flash flooding over NM Highway 117 between mile markers 44 and 51.
The public reported fast-flowing water and mud crossing over Glen Road just east of Pierce Ferry Road in Meadview.
Mohave County alert gauge camera indicated fast-flowing water over White Hills Road just northeast of Highway 93. Water was over the road for approximately 45 minutes.
Public reported hail up to the size of quarters in Pine.
Quarter size hail reported by a former NWS Employee.

A NWS Employee reported flash flooding stretching from San Pedro Creek at NM 14 where the creek was out of its banks. Numerous spots along NM 14 between Cedar Crest and the county line were flooded with rocks and debris over the road, with the worst of it at Ponderosa Park near Lantern Ridge. A USGS gage along the Tijeras Arroyo also observed a nine foot spike to 10 feet, coupled with a report of the arroyo overtopping Via Sedillo Road by two feet. The road was nearly impassible due to large rocks covering the roadway. Damage is an estimate.

Heavy rain in the Paria River drainage resulted in the development and propagation of a flood wave. Approximately 2 miles below the White House campground a group of hikers required helicopter evacuation.
An mPING report was submitted of Sycamore Creek overflowing across Fire Control Road (Nf-64) near Pine.
Hueco Tanks reported 1.54 inches of rain which caused flash flooding at the state park causing the road out to be blocked and visitors stranded.
A trained spotter reported a water rise greater than 4 feet in normally dry Big Bug Creek.
